ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Below the circuit is a common reference line. The left side is labeled input voltage Ui. At the top, a +6 V power supply is connected through resistor R1 to the middle node, denoted as node A. The left side of node A is connected to the input terminal through ideal diode VD1; the right side of node A is connected to the right-side output node through ideal diode VD2, denoted as node B. Node B is connected downward through resistor R2 to the positive terminal of a +3 V power supply, and the negative terminal of this 3 V power supply is connected to the common reference line. The right side is labeled output voltage Uo, indicating the voltage of node B relative to the lower reference line. Reasoning: When Ui > 6 V, according to the direction of VD1 in the figure, the input terminal being higher than the +6 V bias will drive node A to a high potential not lower than +6 V. If VD2 does not conduct, node B will be connected to the +3 V power supply through R2, so node B is +3 V. In the figure, the anode of VD2 is at node B and the cathode is at node A; at this time B = 3 V, while A ≥ 6 V, so VD2 is reverse biased and does not conduct. After VD2 is cut off, there is no current in R2, so there is no voltage drop across R2, and node B is equal to the potential of the 3 V reference power supply. Therefore the output voltage Uo = 3 V.

method.method_draft: First describe the image topology. Let the R1/diode junction be node A and the output node be node B. From the text, the diodes are ideal and Ui > 6 V. With the shown VD1 orientation, Ui greater than the +6 V bias makes node A not less than +6 V, effectively driven high. Node B, if VD2 is not conducting, is held at +3 V through R2 and the 3 V source. Since VD2’s anode is at B and cathode is at A, B = 3 V is lower than A ≥ 6 V, so VD2 is reverse-biased and remains open. Therefore no current flows through R2, no voltage drops on R2, and Uo equals the 3 V reference.

Because Ui > 6 V and the central node is also tied through R1 to +6 V, node A is driven above the 3 V reference level. Test whether VD2 could be on: if VD2 were on, ideal conduction would require B = A, hence B would be above 3 V.
